opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees max out at write, and admin would require the role to own Payroll (Payroll Specialist), which does not apply. Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E045 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read access, and admin is never allowed. The requested write level for Payroll is above the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on a material fact: employment type. Note 1 (HR) lists E045 as full-time, which would allow write; Note 2 (Security) lists E045 as a contractor with basic security training, which caps access at read and never allows admin. Given the conflicting evidence, I apply the more restrictive interpretation consistent with the Security database: contractor with basic training, so the maximum allowable access to Payroll is read. Granting read is safe under policy and never exceeds the requested level.
